sentences.text:
======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr.Md. Harun Quareshi, Advocate
 For the Respondent/s : Mr.Anand Mohan Prasad Mehta, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Shailendra Singh
 Oral Order

2. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 08.08.2022 and order of sentence dated 17.08.2022 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Bhagalpur in connection with S.T. Case No. 245 of 2019 arising out of Tatarpur P.S. Case No. 187 of 2018 whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced for the said offences.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant presses the prayer for bail made by the appellant in the memo of appeal under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.
4.

The main submissions advanced by learned Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3922 of 2022(5)
dt.18-09-2023 counsel for the appellant are that the alleged offence of section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, under which the appellant has been convicted, is not made out against him as the alleged physical relationship between the appellant and the so-called victim was consensual and the same clearly appears from the victim's own evidence discussed in the judgment impugned and the Md. entities.text: Md. Ali @ Md. Ali Khan vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: first alleged occurrence is stated to have taken place on 19.06.2018 but the FIR was lodged on 01.09.2018 after the appellant and his family members denied to marry the victim and in this regard the evidence of PW-2 may be perused and the same is sufficient to show that the FIR of the instant matter was lodged by the victim in order to create pressure upon the appellant to marry her.

Further submissions are that the appellant has been languishing in jail since 08.08.2022 and there is no chance of early hearing of this appeal and as per the medical board's opinion, the victim's age was above 18 years at the time of her examination by the medical board and no sign of recent sexual intercourse was found by the medical board.
5. Learned APP has opposed the bail prayer of the appellant.
6. Considering the above submissions as well as taking into account grounds taken by the appellant as discussed Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3922 of 2022(5) dt.18-09-2023 above, this court is inclined to accept the bail prayer of the appellant.

Accordingly, let the appellant named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Bhagalpur in connection with S.T. Case No. 245 of 2019 arising out of Tatarpur P.S. Case No. 187 of 2018.
7. The sentence of fine shall remain stayed during pendency of this appeal.
8. List this appeal under appropriate heading in due course.
(Shailendra Singh, J) Rajiv/-
